content:
Not all power banks are created equal. Some of the designs out there are honestly some of the most impressive I’ve ever come across, with built-in displays, the ability to charge two MacBooks at once, RGB lighting, and dual transparent windows on the metal housing that show off the internals — Sharge’s new Shargeek 300 power bank is truly a sight to behold, and you really should check it out while it’s available at launch deal pricing. Here are some hands-on impressions.

Sharge Shargeek 300 power bank review

The all-new Sharge Shargeek 300 power bank arrives with a unibody metal chassis, packs a 24,000mAh battery capacity, and can deliver up to 300W of power to your devices. The translucent design, RGB lighting, and built-in display are genuine highlights, and you can pick one up right now on Amazon for the launch deal price of $199.

Feature overview:

  • 300W total output — charge 2 laptops + 1 smartphone simultaneously
  • CNC aluminum alloy body with an advanced thermal system
  • 24,000mAh battery capacity — fully airline-compliant
  • Dual USB-C, USB-A, plus an adjustable DC output (5V-28V)
  • Powers Starlink, portable fridges, soldering irons, camera monitors, cinematography LED lights, and other DC-powered gear
  • 140W USB-C input — Shargeek 300 goes from 0% to 100% in just 44 minutes
  • Full-tab battery cells — operating temperatures reduced by up to 35%
  • 1.9-inch smart display with Sentinel BMS — real-time charge and discharge curves, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage history, and estimated time remaining

9to5Toys take

Sharge is an underrated brand. The charging gear they put out is some of the best-designed around, and the new Shargeek 300 power bank is a perfect example.

This thing is an absolute beauty. Not everyone is going to love what you could call the cyberpunk-style translucent design that exposes the internal components, paired with RGB lighting and a built-in display, but I’m a huge fan, and I’d bet you’ll fall in love with it once you get your hands on it.

What you’re looking at here is a CNC metal unibody build — the vast majority of mainstream competitors in the power bank space with displays use plastic housing… something I’m fairly disgusted by, which is why I really appreciate Sharge’s design ethos. It’s built like a tank.

By my standards, this is an incredibly cool-looking piece of gear — beautiful enough that I’d absolutely keep it on display at the office.

The brand’s products have never let me down and have never failed, and if you haven’t been paying attention to them, they really deserve a spot on your radar. The same has held true during the roughly month or so I’ve been testing the Shargeek 300W power bank.

As for the power output breakdown, you’re looking at a total of 300W here. When all three USB ports are in use, the two primary USB-C ports can deliver 140W simultaneously, while the legacy USB-A port adds another 20W. That’s more than enough to charge three devices at once for me, since I rarely need more than one or two devices while out and about.

Sharge says that when charging via USB-C1 or USB-C2 on its own, it can take your MacBook Pro from “0% to roughly 50% in around 25 to 30 minutes.” In my testing, that figure was bang on — my 14-inch Pro went from nearly dead to just over 50% in 27 minutes.

Alright, let’s talk about the display. I genuinely love this aesthetic — it has a retro yet super modern feel to it, and I’m really into it.

As for functionality, it pretty much shows anything anyone could ever want to know, and plenty more that I don’t need to know — real-time charging status, some discharge curves that I’m not overly invested in but love looking at, individual cell voltages, cycle count, usage history, and all sorts of data. From what I’ve seen, everything works incredibly smoothly, and more importantly, every time I pull it out to use it, it makes me feel like I’m in the world of Blade Runner or Cyberpunk 2077.

For power nerds and the professionals who actually know what to do with all this charging and voltage analytics data, this is the most comprehensive set of power data I’ve ever seen on a consumer-grade power bank.

Well, I’ve found my new favorite power bank. It performs as well as it looks, and it’s going to remain a staple in my daily carry for the foreseeable future.
